newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt calls time on official speeding.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt calls time on official speeding.

text.p: The Czech government on Wednesday rescinded Communist-era traffic rules which allowed party officials to break speed limits at will in town.
Top Communist party members and selected officials displayed so-called S-Cards on their cars giving them a clear run in the fast lane.
The government also also raised the speed limit on four-lane motorways to 130 kph (80 mph) from 110 kph (70 mph), Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said.
Lower Czech speed limits on motorways have been in effect since the communist era when the vast majority of cars were low-powered Skodas and Russian-made Ladas.
Since the 1989 revolution and the turn to a market economy, the number of high-powered western cars on the roads has risen substantially, as have the number of accidents and deaths.
